label: MODEL_ONLY / FORECAST_ONLY / NOT_MEASURED_IN_THIS_SYSTEM
scope: Agent-substrate and governance requirements R21-R59, as enumerated in the full-system completion directive. The scientific requirements of the earlier sections are governed by authorities.json and are not restated here.
rule: A row may not be classified above PARTIALLY_IMPLEMENTED without tests, nor COMPLETE_TO_CURRENT_TECHNICALLY_DEFENSIBLE_LIMIT without mutation coverage AND an empty residual_gaps list. tools/completion_matrix.py enforces every mechanically checkable claim; tests/test_completion_matrix.py runs it in CI.
does_not_mean: A complete row means the SOFTWARE requirement is met to the current technically defensible limit. It says nothing about scientific validity. PASS remains 0 and no row here can change that.

rows.requirement: Tool execution as a full subsystem: identity, contract, schemas, capability, limits, timeout, cancellation, provenance
rows.persistent_state: task.execution events record outcome, tool id, version and contract digest, exit status, signal number, stdout/stderr digests, the limits applied and the duration
rows.evidence: ExecutionResult carries tool digest, exit status, signal, stdout/stderr digests and byte counts, duration and the limits actually applied
rows.provenance: tool_id, version and contract digest cited by every result
rows.failure_semantics: five outcomes; TIMED_OUT, CANCELLED and DENIED are each distinct from FAILED and none of them is success
rows.recovery: the execution record is durable, so a crash after it is recoverable; a crash before it leaves the job's lease to lapse and scheduler.reconcile returns the work to READY
rows.retry: RETRYABLE is TIMED_OUT|CANCELLED; a deterministic rejection is not retryable
rows.cancellation: CancellationToken checked before spawn and during the wait
rows.concurrency: one execution per job, under an unexpired scheduler lease
rows.security_boundary: registry default-deny; capability checked against a log-projected ledger before execution; kernel rlimits; own process group; a BUILT environment rather than an inherited one; a default-deny egress guard around the call
residual_gaps: one registered tool, invoked by one workflow
no output-file collection declared in the contract; the caller captures the directory instead
retry is the scheduler's -- classified, capped, in seq units. The executor has no retry loop and no idle timeout: a tool that writes one byte a minute runs to its wall bound
the contract declares SideEffect.EXTERNAL and nothing consumes that declaration; there are no compensating actions
the egress guard binds THIS process, not the child. A subprocess that opens its own socket is not stopped by it; nothing here is containment

rows.requirement: Default deny for tool, filesystem, network, secret and external-service authority
rows.persistent_state: network.grant / network.request / network.result and secret.grant / secret.access events; the governed run holds zero egress grants and the Snakefile asserts it
rows.evidence: refusals are raised AND, for network and secrets, recorded: a control plane that logs only what it permitted cannot answer 'what did this agent try'
rows.provenance: every network request and secret access names actor, task and purpose
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed, with a distinct exception per authority
rows.recovery: none
rows.security_boundary: filesystem writes allowlisted at the write primitive; tool execution default-deny; egress default-deny with label-wise host matching and address pinning; secrets held by reference and rendered as placeholders
rows.fuzzing: tools/fuzz_substrate.py covers netauth grant and target parsing
residual_gaps: READ paths are gated for the governed workflow and the evidence store; reads made by code that does not go through GovernedReader are still ungoverned, and nothing forces a future caller to use it
no external-service authority beyond egress: no per-service identity, quota or contract
the egress guard is in-process and reversible by code inside the block; it is mediation, not a sandbox -- and so is the read boundary

rows.persistent_state: outcome, exit status and signal are durable in the task.execution event; the job's lease and state are durable in scheduler.transition events
rows.evidence: real exit status and signal number recorded separately
rows.provenance: tool id, version and contract digest cited by every result
rows.failure_semantics: a signalled death is not an exit status; a timeout is not a failure of the tool and not a success; a run is now bounded by IDLENESS as well as by wall time -- a tool that stops producing output is abandoned rather than held to the wall bound, because 'how long may this take' is the wrong question for work that has stopped making progress
rows.recovery: partial output from a killed process is captured and hashed; a supervisor crash leaves the lease to lapse and scheduler.reconcile returns the work to READY; the child's pid and process-group id are recorded in the execution record the moment the child exists, so a supervisor that dies mid-run leaves an orphan that something can still name and signal. They are diagnostic and the record says so: a pid identifies only on the host that produced it and only until it is reused, which is why the run's start time sits beside it
rows.cancellation: terminate the group, grace, then kill
rows.security_boundary: setsid process group; never signals its own group
residual_gaps: the recorded pid is diagnostic, not a handle: nothing automatically signals an orphan on the next supervisor's behalf, and a pid is meaningful only on the host that produced it and only until reuse

the idle bound measures OUTPUT, because that is the only progress signal this executor has. A tool thinking hard and silently is indistinguishable from one that has deadlocked; the wall bound is what covers that case

descendants are TERMINATED by the process-group kill but not REAPED: a grandchild whose parent is gone becomes a zombie until init collects it, which is measured rather than assumed -- an earlier wording said such a grandchild 'outlives its parent', and what actually survives is a process-table entry, not a running process

rows.requirement: Durable task/job lifecycle with centralized transitions
rows.persistent_state: task state is a projection of the hash-chained log
rows.evidence: every transition records the edge's reason
rows.provenance: actor and role on every transition record
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed; FAILED, TIMED_OUT and CANCELLED are distinct states, and VERIFIED is reachable only from COMPLETED
rows.recovery: projection() replays the log, so state survives the process
rows.retry: FAILED and TIMED_OUT have explicit edges back to QUEUED
rows.idempotency: not yet: a resubmitted task is a new task
rows.concurrency: leases; optimistic only, no multi-process test
rows.security_boundary: separation of duties between executor and verifier
residual_gaps: idempotency keys are the SCHEDULER's; task.create carries none, so a resubmission is deduplicated at the queue and not at the task record
a crash between the execution record and the COMPLETED transition leaves the task EXECUTING: the lease lapses and reconcile requeues the JOB, but nothing automatically resolves the task record
concurrency is tested across processes on one host; two hosts against shared storage, where advisory locking is a weaker guarantee, is not tested

rows.persistent_state: lease recorded on the task, expiring by log seq
rows.evidence: none
rows.provenance: none
rows.failure_semantics: LeaseError for wrong holder, wrong lease id, or lapse
rows.recovery: expired_leases() lists stranded work; requeue drops the lease
rows.concurrency: single holder; takeover only after expiry, and a requeue claiming a lapse is refused on replay when the lease is still live
rows.security_boundary: an outcome may be reported only by the lease holder, only while the lease is live, and this is re-derived on replay from the state the replay reached -- not only refused at the write path, where it was advice a forged record walked around
residual_gaps: no lease RENEWAL: a worker holding long work cannot extend, so a lease must be sized for the worst case rather than the common one
lease expiry is in sequence numbers, so a lease on an idle log never lapses in wall time -- deterministic, and not what 'expires' suggests
split-brain is tested with real concurrent processes on one host; shared network storage, where flock is weaker, is not tested

rows.persistent_state: scheduler.enqueue / scheduler.transition / scheduler.priority events; the whole queue is a projection
rows.authority_owner: Scheduler.readiness (dependencies, evidence, capability, capacity, policy) and check_edge
rows.evidence: requires_evidence digests must resolve through a caller-supplied resolver before dispatch; the governed Stage-10 run is dispatched through the scheduler and its outcome reported to it; the Snakemake rule fails unless the job reaches SUCCEEDED
rows.provenance: every readiness verdict, requeue, retry and cancellation is an event carrying its reason
rows.failure_semantics: eight job states with a derived SEALED set; a permanently FAILED, CANCELLED or INVALIDATED job blocks everything transitively downstream at the moment it finishes, rather than leaving dependents WAITING until reconcile next runs
rows.recovery: restart reloads the queue from the log; reconcile requeues lapsed leases and is idempotent
rows.retry: classified by FailureClass; only TRANSIENT, TIMEOUT and RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED are retryable, with capped exponential backoff in sequence numbers
rows.idempotency: an idempotency key returns the original job for identical work and is refused for different work
rows.cancellation: cancel cascades transitively by default; a terminal failure cascades to BLOCKED, distinguishing a decision from a failure because an operator responds to the two differently
rows.concurrency: leases with sequence-number expiry, optimistic revisions, and capacity bounds on concurrent dispatch
rows.security_boundary: policy-gated enqueue, dispatch, cancellation and priority escalation; a stale or foreign lease may not report an outcome, and the REPLAY re-derives that from its own state: ownership, lease liveness, the attempt count and whether a requeue's claimed lapse is true. Those refusals lived only on the write path, so a rejected report could be appended directly and the next load called the job SUCCEEDED
property_tests: tests/test_agent_machine_properties.py (SchedulerMachine: readiness, the cancellation cascade, lease presence, retry budget, and a fresh replay equal to the live projection, checked after every step)
rows.fuzzing: tools/fuzz_substrate.py fuzzes job_from_record, so a malformed durable job record is refused rather than projected
residual_gaps: the governed path enqueues ONE job per run, so dependency graphs and multi-job scheduling are exercised only in tests and in the long-horizon workload, never by a real caller

no wall-clock scheduling at all: every deadline, lease and backoff is in sequence numbers. That is what makes the queue reproducible after a restart, and it means a lease on an idle log never lapses in real time
one queue in one process. There is no distributed dispatch, no work stealing, and the advisory lock that serializes writers is a weaker guarantee on shared network storage than on a local filesystem

rows.persistent_state: agent.register / agent.retire / agent.message / agent.claim / agent.escalation events; the directory is a projection
rows.evidence: each identity has a content digest over agent id, instance id, kind and roles; the governed run requires registered worker and verifier identities and runs check_separation between them; replay re-authorizes every transition from the state IT reached, so presence in the log is never authority
rows.provenance: who registered whom, and for a HUMAN principal the chain back to the out-of-band bootstrap
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed: an unregistered instance did not participate; an unregistered prior role-holder is treated as the SAME party rather than a different one
rows.recovery: the directory reloads from the log; a duplicate registration, a duplicate escalation or a redelivery that changes a body each refuse the load
rows.idempotency: one registration per instance; a second is refused rather than widening roles
rows.cancellation: retirement takes effect at its own event, not after it
rows.security_boundary: incompatible role pairs cannot be held by one identity, and two runs of one agent are ONE party for separation of duties
residual_gaps: identity is not authenticated; instance_id is a name the registrar chose
no cryptographic binding between an instance and the actions attributed to it
identity is still not authenticated on the production path

rows.requirement: Human authority and escalation as workflow states
rows.persistent_state: agent.register / agent.retire / agent.message / agent.claim / agent.escalation events; the directory is a projection
rows.evidence: the answer, the option set it was checked against, and the answerer's reason
rows.provenance: who raised it, who answered, why, and at which log position
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed and PERMANENTLY so here: an escalation blocks its task until a human answers, and this repository contains no human decision
rows.recovery: the directory reloads from the log; a duplicate registration, a duplicate escalation or a redelivery that changes a body each refuse the load
rows.idempotency: an answered escalation cannot be answered again
rows.security_boundary: no agent may answer an escalation whatever roles it holds, and no agent may register a HUMAN principal; the bootstrap is a spelled-out constant so granting human authority is greppable
residual_gaps: a human cannot be authenticated here; PrincipalKind.HUMAN is a property of a registration record and the module says so
no notification channel -- an open escalation is visible by query, not delivered
the governed path raises no escalation, because nothing in a Stage-10 artifact run is a decision a human must make

rows.persistent_state: policy.publish events; documents are projected from the verified log
rows.evidence: each Decision carries the deciding document's content digest, not only its id; the governed run publishes stage10.governed, consults it, and records the decision; a DENY rule stops the run before any task record exists
rows.provenance: policy.decision events record allowed AND denied requests with the rule that decided, and each is RE-EVALUATED on load against the document in force at that position: a record whose verdict, effect or rule the rules do not produce refuses the load rather than being repeated by every reader downstream
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed: unpublished policy authorizes nothing; no matching rule denies; empty match fields refused at construction
rows.recovery: PolicyStore.load rebuilds every version from the log; a version gap, a document whose content does not match its recorded digest, or a decision the rules of the day would not have reached, refuses the load
rows.idempotency: n/a: publication is versioned, and a version may not be reused
rows.concurrency: versions are gap-free and append-ordered; a second writer's publication is refused unless it follows the version it read
rows.security_boundary: deny-overrides so a prohibition cannot be defeated by ordering; in_force_at makes decisions non-retroactive (I5)
residual_gaps: no fuzzing of policy records
no obligations/constraints on an ALLOW decision, only a boolean verdict

rows.persistent_state: capability.issue / capability.revoke events; the in-force set is a projection of them, not a caller's variable
rows.evidence: every grant names subject, task, tool, scope and expiry
rows.provenance: capability_from_record rebuilds a grant from its log payload; the ledger refuses one id issued twice with different terms
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed; distinct exceptions for unknown, revoked, expired and denied
rows.recovery: rebuilt by replaying the log; a lost projection costs time, never authority
rows.concurrency: issuance appends through the log's writer lock; revocation takes effect for every later check
rows.security_boundary: a grant is bounded in subject, task, action, tool and path scope, and in a validity WINDOW closed at both ends: expiry was checked and issuance was not, so a capability recorded at seq 90 answered 'was this permitted at seq 20' with yes. The ledger stamps the start from the log and refuses a record that names its own
residual_gaps: subject is not authenticated; a grant cannot be used under another name but nothing proves who a name belongs to
no ISSUER authority: any actor that can write the log can mint a grant. issuer_of() records who did, and is deliberately not consulted by check() -- attribution, not authorization
no delegation or attenuation
expiry is in sequence numbers, so a grant does not lapse with wall time on an idle log -- deterministic, and not what an operator expects of 'expires'

rows.requirement: Filesystem authority: immutable evidence vs workspace vs canonical outputs
rows.persistent_state: file.read events: every governed read attempt, permitted or refused, with the identity of the object actually opened
rows.authority_owner: safeio.read_beneath for confinement; readpath.GovernedReader for who may read; workspace.assert_in_workspace for writes
rows.evidence: the authorized root is opened ONCE as a directory descriptor and every component is opened descriptor-relative with O_NOFOLLOW, so a symlink anywhere on the path is refused rather than followed; O_NONBLOCK on the final open means a substituted FIFO is refused instead of hanging; the OPENED object is fstat-ed and must be a regular file within bounds; and an expected digest binds the result to CONTENT rather than to a name
rows.provenance: each read records actor, task, capability, root, requested resource, the (device, inode) actually opened and the digest of the bytes -- never the bytes
rows.failure_semantics: default deny: a reader with no capability reads nothing; every refusal names which check refused
rows.recovery: append-only store; no delete path
rows.concurrency: the descriptor is bound to an inode, so rename, replace or unlink after the open cannot redirect the read
rows.security_boundary: confinement enforced at the OPEN, not by validating a string a later caller re-opens. Mediation, not containment: a process that calls open() itself is unaffected
rows.fuzzing: tools/fuzz_substrate.py targets read_path and read_beneath: the path parser and an actual confined read against a real root
residual_gaps: HARD LINKS are not detectable: a name inside the root may be a hard link to content elsewhere on the same filesystem, and O_NOFOLLOW says nothing about it because a hard link is not a link. Where the identity of the bytes matters the caller passes a digest; where it does not, this is a real hole and not a theoretical one

openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH) would make confinement a single atomic kernel decision rather than a per-component walk. This Python exposes neither os.openat2 nor os.RESOLVE_BENEATH, so the walk is the strongest form available here -- an unavailable platform primitive, not unfinished engineering
bind mounts and overlays are not detectable portably: if the root itself is a mount somebody else controls, confinement to it means less than it appears to
case-insensitive filesystems are out of scope; the targets are case-sensitive and nothing here consults the root's own semantics
no disk-full injection on the read path (there is nothing to write), and permission-error injection is covered for the evidence store only

rows.persistent_state: network.grant / network.request / network.result events; grants are projected from the verified log
rows.authority_owner: NetworkAuthority.authorize (default deny) and socket_guard at the process layer
rows.evidence: each decision carries the deciding grant's content digest; the governed run executes inside a socket guard with no egress grant, and a connection attempted during execution is refused
rows.provenance: every attempt is recorded with actor, task, tool, capability and destination -- refusals included, payloads never
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed: no grant means no network; NetworkDenied deliberately does not subclass OSError so a retry loop cannot swallow a policy decision
rows.recovery: grants reload from the log; a grant record whose content does not match its recorded digest refuses the load
rows.cancellation: revocation takes effect at the next authorize call
rows.concurrency: the socket guard is process-wide for the duration of its block and is removed in a finally
rows.security_boundary: label-wise host matching (no prefix/suffix confusion), explicit scheme/port/method/path, separate address classes for loopback and private ranges, address pinning against DNS rebinding, userinfo refusal; the grant's window is closed at both ends and its start is stamped from the log, and a second record naming a live grant_id with different terms is refused rather than silently replacing authority already in force. A body carrying a registered secret is refused unless a secret grant names egress to that host -- checked by value, because the leak that matters is a credential under an innocent name
residual_gaps: kernel-level containment (network namespace, seccomp, firewall) is NOT provided and is documented as absent; in-process code can restore socket.connect
no fuzzing of URL parsing
ingress is not modelled at all; Direction has one member

rows.requirement: Secret handling: references not inherited environment
rows.persistent_state: secret.grant / secret.access events carry ids, purposes and grant digests; never a value and never a digest of one
rows.evidence: grant digests; deliberately no digest of the value, which would be an offline guessing oracle
rows.provenance: every resolution is recorded with actor, task, tool and purpose
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed: an unregistered secret, an unknown grant, a revoked or expired grant, or a purpose mismatch each raise rather than returning an empty value
rows.recovery: grants are in the log; values are process-local by design and are re-supplied by the deployment, never persisted here
rows.cancellation: revocation takes effect at the next reveal, not when the last handle is collected
rows.security_boundary: reference/value separation, placeholder rendering through str/repr/format, value-based redaction across every output surface, an explicit egress-composition check against the confused deputy, and a governed tool environment that inherits nothing; a secret grant does not reach backwards over a read that happened before it was issued. The confused deputy -- a component that legitimately holds a credential for A and legitimately holds egress to B, persuaded to send the first to the second -- is now checked at the BOUNDARY rather than by a function nobody called. check_egress_composition had no caller outside its own tests; it is now reached two ways: Secret.reveal_for(decision) checks the pairing before the plaintext exists, and NetworkAuthority.authorize refuses by VALUE when a body carries a registered secret no grant pairs with that host
residual_gaps: no secret is resolved on the production path, because nothing there needs one -- the governed tool's environment is BUILT from a declared allowlist rather than inherited, so a credential in os.environ cannot reach it at all
redaction finds the value and the enumerated encodings only; a hashed, encrypted, compressed or split derivative is not detectable and the module says so
zeroing a bytearray does not guarantee no copy remains; str is immutable and the interpreter may have copied it
no external secret provider integration (file, keyring, cloud)

the pairing check is mediation: a component holding both grants can still call reveal() and write its own socket, which reaches neither the composed operation nor the egress boundary. The value-based check is the stronger of the two because it does not depend on the caller choosing the safe method, and it still only sees bodies that come through authorize()

rows.requirement: Context lifecycle as a controlled subsystem
rows.persistent_state: context.build events carry the manifest -- digests, tiers, lengths and omissions -- and never the assembled text
rows.authority_owner: ContextBuilder.build; MANDATORY tiers cannot be dropped
rows.evidence: every item is named by the digest of the exact bytes shown; the governed run builds and records a context manifest whose digest is written into governed_run.json
rows.provenance: the manifest answers which policy version and which evidence were available, and what was available and NOT shown
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed: mandatory material that does not fit raises ContextBudgetError rather than being dropped
rows.recovery: manifests round-trip from the log; an unknown field refuses the read
rows.security_boundary: a redactor may be attached, and a context containing a registered secret value is refused; ContextItem has no field the text could be stored in
residual_gaps: model-output reproducibility is explicitly NOT provided; sampling and model version are not captured
no token-based budgeting, only bytes -- a byte budget is a proxy for a token budget and the two differ per tokenizer

rows.requirement: Read-only evidence retrieval that cannot mutate authority
rows.persistent_state: serialized index treated as a cache, verified against source
rows.evidence: every hit carries path, line range, source digest and evidence_status=RETRIEVED_TEXT_NOT_EVIDENCE
rows.provenance: file_digests + per-chunk source spans
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed ValueError on stale-or-forged index
rows.recovery: rebuild from source
rows.security_boundary: path traversal, absolute, symlink, duplicate, excluded-tree, suffix and root-escape guards; k bounded
residual_gaps: corpus membership is git-tracked-file equality, not a signed allowlist
no fuzzing of the index document parser

rows.requirement: Durable agent memory separated from evidence and authority
rows.persistent_state: memory.write / memory.status events; entries are projected from the verified log
rows.authority_owner: none, deliberately: memory influences proposals and decides nothing
rows.evidence: an entry names what it was derived from, and a citation that does not resolve in the evidence store is refused at write time; the governed run files a note citing its artifacts, and the Snakemake rule fails if that note's digest resolves as evidence
rows.provenance: author, sources, supersession and the reason for every status change
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed on fabricated citations, duplicate ids, empty or oversized entries, and unknown record fields
rows.recovery: entries reload from the log; a duplicate write refuses the load
rows.idempotency: one write per memory_id; a second is refused rather than replacing the first
rows.cancellation: retraction by the author only; the text stays in the log and the status changes
rows.security_boundary: structural: a memory digest never enters the evidence store so it cannot satisfy I6, and no module in the authority path may import this one -- enforced by the layering test; a status a replay would refuse does not become state: the status machine and the authorship rule are enforced on REPLAY as well as on the write path
residual_gaps: memory is not retrievable through the RAG index, so the 'retrievable memory keeps its lower authority' case is unimplemented rather than solved
no bound on total memory size across entries, only per entry

rows.requirement: Multi-agent identity, message provenance and conflict handling
rows.persistent_state: agent.register / agent.retire / agent.message / agent.claim / agent.escalation events; the directory is a projection
rows.evidence: claims name their value by digest, so two claims are compared without comparing prose; worker and verifier are distinct registered instances and the separation between them is checked by the directory
rows.provenance: messages are identified, attributed, ordered by the log and append-only
rows.failure_semantics: an unresolved conflict is an explicit outcome; there is deliberately no LAST_WRITER_WINS rule
rows.recovery: the directory reloads from the log; a duplicate registration, a duplicate escalation or a redelivery that changes a body each refuse the load
rows.retry: duplicate message delivery is a no-op; a redelivery that changes the body is refused
rows.cancellation: messages for a superseded task are refused and reported, without stopping delivery of the ones behind them
rows.concurrency: ordering is the log's; a retired recipient's messages are not delivered to a successor
rows.security_boundary: an instance cannot act under another's identity, cannot claim in a role it does not hold, and cannot manufacture a quorum by repeating itself; the human gate is enforced on replay: an appended agent.escalation.answer cannot record a decision no person made, by a non-human principal, by the asker, outside the offered options, or over one already recorded
residual_gaps: no transport: the bus is a projection of one shared log, which assumes every party can write to it
REQUIRE_HUMAN is unsatisfiable in this repository, by design, because no human decision exists here

rows.persistent_state: none (pure replay)
rows.evidence: Divergence tuples
rows.provenance: none
rows.failure_semantics: refuses a broken log
rows.recovery: rebuilds state from the log alone
rows.security_boundary: none
residual_gaps: separation is implementation-level only: same process, same language, same canonical-form module
no separate-process or separate-dependency verifier

rows.persistent_state: append-only log is the commit point
rows.evidence: hash-chained records
rows.provenance: none
rows.failure_semantics: the enforcement projection refuses a history it cannot authorize rather than handing back a partial state; the independent replay records the problem and continues, so one bad record does not hide the rest
rows.recovery: every prefix of a governed run is swept: the chain still verifies, the projection either succeeds or refuses, the two readers agree, and no prefix yields a VERIFIED task without the execution and evidence records behind it. Each state a crash can leave a task in has a named recovery, and a state with no entry fails the test
rows.idempotency: idempotency keys on the scheduler; the log's append is the commit point, so a crash before it leaves no trace and a crash after it leaves a durable record the next load replays
rows.security_boundary: none
residual_gaps: the governed path is NOT one atomic unit and there is no two-phase commit. What is established instead is that every PREFIX is a state recovery handles, and which prefixes produce each state

a crash between the execution record and the COMPLETED transition still leaves the task EXECUTING. The lease lapses and the scheduler requeues the WORK, but nothing automatically resolves the task RECORD -- the sweep pins down exactly which prefixes do this rather than leaving it as prose
no compensating actions for non-rollbackable effects; the tool contract declares SideEffect.EXTERNAL and nothing consumes that declaration

rows.persistent_state: JSONL log + separately witnessed head
rows.evidence: hash chain + head witness
rows.provenance: actor, action, target, wall_time per record
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed; structured VerifyReport, never a bare bool
rows.recovery: corrupt-tail detection; truncation caught by the witness
rows.concurrency: an exclusive flock on a sidecar lock file serializes the whole verify-and-append section across processes; measured before the fix, four concurrent writers produced four records at seq 0 and corrupted the chain permanently
rows.security_boundary: none
residual_gaps: the writer lock is POSIX advisory: a process that opens the file directly is not stopped, and flock over NFS is unreliable -- both stated in the module
no segmentation or rotation, so full verification is O(n) in history forever
no schema version on an event record, so a newer writer's fields are refused rather than migrated

rows.persistent_state: checkpoint files + snapshot blobs in the evidence store
rows.evidence: snapshot pinned by content digest
rows.provenance: full_verification flag travels with the checkpoint
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed; refuses to checkpoint a log that does not verify
rows.recovery: latest_usable walks back past unusable checkpoints
rows.security_boundary: none
residual_gaps: self-hash detects corruption, NOT tampering — no authentication
no cleanup or retention policy for old checkpoints
concurrent checkpoint-while-appending is untested

rows.requirement: Independent state reconstruction covering every event type
rows.persistent_state: none
rows.evidence: none
rows.provenance: none
rows.failure_semantics: fail-closed on an action nothing in this package writes; another subsystem's action is counted as foreign rather than treated as damage
rows.recovery: none
rows.security_boundary: none
rows.differential: compare(store, recon) over generated histories, and compare_tasks(projection, recon) over governed runs and over forged ones
residual_gaps: the independent reconstruction rebuilds AUTHORITY RECORDS and TASKS. Scheduler, policy, memory, agent, network, secret and context state have no second implementation
no differential comparison for those subsystems, so their projections are checked against themselves

rows.persistent_state: STALE transitions recorded in the log
rows.evidence: explain() returns the dependency path
rows.provenance: none
rows.failure_semantics: cycle-tolerant; reports rather than looping
rows.recovery: none
rows.security_boundary: none
residual_gaps: dependencies are explicit record-to-record edges only; nothing derives them from real scientific inputs

rows.persistent_state: none; a view over the log
rows.evidence: every step names actor, action, tool, version and digests; and the queries are a committed COMMAND (tools/audit_log.py) that CI runs over the governed run's own log immediately after the rule writes it, failing the build when the answer is a finding rather than printing it into a log nobody reads
rows.provenance: the chain IS the provenance record
